October 14, 2026

Russian strikes cut power to hundreds of thousands in Ukraine as Starlink access falters

tags: war, politics, tech
sources: @aaronparnas, @hunteralexanderhowell

President Volodymyr Zelensky said overnight Russian attacks on the Kyiv region involved large numbers of drones and more than 39 ballistic missiles, striking energy sites and leaving an estimated 600,000 people without power despite a declared energy ceasefire. Ukrainian military officials and an adviser to Zelensky said Elon Musk was deliberately disrupting Ukrainian access to Starlink terminals, which would degrade the country's ability to coordinate its defences. The reported cutoff comes as the United States scales back support for Kyiv.

Ukraine hits Russian oil depot days after Trump told it to stop

tags: war, politics
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell

More than 500 Ukrainian drones struck a Russian oil depot overnight, setting it ablaze. It is the first Ukrainian strike on Russian energy infrastructure since President Donald Trump publicly instructed Kyiv two days earlier not to target such sites. The strike is being read as a signal of Ukrainian frustration with Washington's position and carries a risk of further escalation.

Trump weighs calling off livestreamed firing-squad execution of Fort Hood shooter

tags: legal, politics, defence
sources: @aaronparnas, @groundnews, @oafnation_actual

The administration is reconsidering plans to broadcast the December 3 execution of Nidal Hasan, the former Army major convicted of killing 13 people at Fort Hood in 2009. CNN reported Trump told advisers he had not known Hasan was paralysed from the waist down, and officials told CBS News they are now leaning against the broadcast the Pentagon had previously announced. House Speaker Mike Johnson warned the footage could become a recruiting tool for terrorist groups, and Republican Senators Lisa Murkowski and Thom Tillis condemned the broadcast plan while still supporting the execution. It would be the first US military execution by firing squad since 1945.

US inflation rises to 3.7% in September, above forecasts

tags: economy, markets, politics
sources: @groundnews

Consumer price inflation climbed to 3.7% in September from 3.4% in August, exceeding economists' expectations and landing weeks before the November midterm elections. Higher gasoline prices drove much of the increase after the US-Israel war with Iran disrupted Middle Eastern oil supplies, pushing crude from around $70 a barrel before the conflict to more than $100. Research from the Federal Reserve Bank of New York found tariffs also contributed, with US businesses absorbing nearly 90% of tariff costs as consumer prices rose.

Judge orders halt to $20 million taxpayer-funded ad campaign promoting Trump

tags: legal, politics
sources: @groundnews

US District Judge Jennifer Rochon barred further spending on a nearly $20 million advertising campaign promoting President Trump ahead of the midterm elections, finding the ads likely violate federal law. The campaign drew on funds designated for US Customs and Border Protection, and the order requires cancellation of remaining advertisements, including those scheduled for October 11. Common Cause, labor unions and a Democratic state legislative candidate brought the suit, arguing taxpayer money was misused for political advertising; the administration argued the case was unnecessary because the campaign was ending. The ruling lasts two weeks and is the first court order blocking the campaign.

Opposition to data centers spreads across party lines, including among Texas Republicans

tags: tech, climate, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Texas Republicans have joined a broader surge of local opposition to data center construction, with resistance now reported in communities across the political spectrum. Recent incidents cited include a spill of 5,000 gallons of diesel from a data center into New Jersey's Hackensack River, heavy water consumption by facilities in Georgia, and persistent noise complaints in Virginia. Data centers powered by fossil fuels are also linked to higher air and carbon pollution, raising public health costs and premature deaths.

New White House press secretary's debut draws internal criticism and scrutiny of her record

tags: politics, media
sources: @aaronparnas, @ericmoutsos, @total.hypocrisy, @hunteralexanderhowell

Katie Zachariah's first briefing as White House press secretary was described by Trump aides as "brutal," with internal questions raised about how long she will remain in the role and whether she is a licensed attorney. In the briefing she declined to say whether the US had stopped sharing intelligence with Ukraine, confirmed that Ambassador Kimberly Guilfoyle had been asked to resign, and described a "historic one-day war" and a "booming economy," claims disputed by commentators who pointed to months of conflict and uneven economic gains. Reporting from OPB noted Zachariah served on the advisory board of an anti-abortion group called the White Rose Resistance, whose founder has publicly advocated expanding the death penalty.

BBC pushes to depose Trump in his own $10 billion lawsuit

tags: legal, media, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Counsel for the BBC said Trump had agreed to sit for a deposition on October 16 in the $10 billion suit he filed against the broadcaster, then withdrew, citing urgent matters of national importance. Trump's side is seeking to delay the deposition until January, after the midterm elections and after discovery in the case closes. The BBC argues the deposition is a necessary part of discovery in a case Trump initiated, and the court has yet to rule.

MI5 warns Iran is expanding efforts to target military bases in Britain

tags: defence, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

MI5 said Iranian efforts to target military installations are widening and that the incident at RAF Fairford was "not unique." The Pentagon withdrew US bombers from the British base after a suspected threat. Seven men were arrested and released on bail, and Britain has pointed to Iran's Revolutionary Guard, which Tehran denies.

Army sends hundreds more troops to Rio Grande Valley over cartel activity

tags: immigration, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

US officials cited signs of elevated cartel activity in ordering hundreds of additional soldiers to the Rio Grande Valley this month. The Coast Guard said it recently encountered gunfire from the Mexican side of the river and returned fire, with no injuries reported. Mexico has deployed 500 National Guard and military personnel to Tamaulipas as cooperation between the two governments increases.

Op-ed argues military could be sorted by political affiliation ahead of domestic deployments

tags: politics, defence
sources: @total.hypocrisy

An independent writer published an opinion piece arguing it would be technically possible, though illegal, for the Pentagon under Secretary Pete Hegseth and newly installed loyalist commanders to sort service members by voter registration. The theory holds that troops registered as Democrats, judged more likely to refuse unlawful orders, could be deployed abroad while others remain stationed domestically. The piece cites reporting in The Atlantic that Trump supporters have urged him to consider martial law, and notes that Congress has voted once to end the war in Iran without effect.

Guilfoyle said to have kept journal of Trump world secrets after being dismissed as ambassador

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

The Daily Mail reported that Kimberly Guilfoyle, removed as ambassador to Greece, kept a journal recording secrets about the Trump family and the wider MAGA movement. Insiders quoted in the report said she "knows where the bodies are buried" and expressed concern she may seek revenge. Trump said publicly that Guilfoyle, formerly engaged to Donald Trump Jr., was never part of his family, a remark seen as raising the likelihood of disclosures.

OpenAI engineer arrested over hidden recording device in executive conference room

tags: legal, tech, surveillance
sources: @groundnews

Abdulrahman Alfozan, a 35-year-old Saudi national employed by OpenAI since July 2025, faces federal charges of attempting to intercept private conversations after a device was found hidden in an executive conference room used for confidential research and business discussions. Employees discovered the device on September 30, concealed in toilet paper and connected to a television's USB port. Prosecutors allege Alfozan researched executive meeting locations, and that a chatbot account linked to his spouse contained queries about building and hiding recording equipment. OpenAI fired him and referred the matter to the FBI, saying it found no evidence of unauthorized access to model weights, source code or customer data.

Trump posts videos of animal attacks on Truth Social, prompting questions about his fitness

tags: politics, media
sources: @aaronparnas

Trump spent an afternoon and overnight hours posting graphic videos of animals attacking and killing people on Truth Social, drawing criticism from some Republicans. He followed with a post casting himself as the man who entered a tiger enclosure in Yorkshire, England, depicting himself subduing the animal. Medical commentators and political figures cited the posts as evidence of concern about the president's state of health.

Endorsement slate targets six Senate and House races deciding control of Congress

tags: politics, environment
sources: @carolinegleich

A set of national midterm endorsements names Mary Peltola in Alaska and Troy Jackson in Maine for the Senate, where Democrats need four additional seats to overturn the Republicans' 53-seat majority. House endorsements cover Manny Rutinel in Colorado's 8th, JoAnna Mendoza in Arizona's 6th, Cait Conley in New York's 17th, and Sam Forstag, a Missoula firefighter running for Ryan Zinke's open western Montana seat. The slate is framed around congressional control of public lands funding and protections. Election Day is Tuesday, November 3.

Utah changes ballot deadline as mail voting rules tighten

tags: politics
sources: @carolinegleich

Utah ballots went out on October 13, and ballots must now physically reach the county clerk by 8 p.m. on November 3, with a postmark no longer sufficient. Voters mailing ballots are advised to allow a full week, and drop boxes remain free to use. The state also has new congressional maps, so district boundaries may have changed; voter registration closes at 5 p.m. on October 23, with in-person same-day registration available with ID.

No Kings rally and march to ballot drop boxes planned in Salt Lake City

tags: politics
sources: @carolinegleich

A "No Kings" rally is scheduled for Saturday, October 17 at 3 p.m. at the Utah State Capitol, followed by a march to the nearest ballot drop box at 4 p.m. Organisers describe it as a peaceful demonstration for democracy and are asking attendees to bring ballots to deposit. The event is framed around turnout for the November midterms.

Gasoline-only cars fall below half of global new-vehicle sales for first time

tags: climate, markets
sources: @groundnews

Gasoline-only vehicles made up 49% of global new-car sales in the first half of 2026, down from 73% in 2021, according to Mobility Global data reported by Nikkei. Gasoline-only sales fell 10% to 20.25 million, while hybrids rose 10% to 7.27 million and battery-electric sales rose 12% to 6.87 million, with rising fuel prices linked to Middle East conflict contributing to the shift. Declines were steepest in China, down 26%, and Europe, down 13%, though about 83% of new vehicles sold worldwide still contain a combustion engine when hybrids are counted.

More than 2 million veterans now hold 100% VA disability ratings

tags: politics, health
sources: @oafnation_actual

Department of Veterans Affairs data shows over 2 million veterans are rated 100% disabled, an increase of 122% since 2021. The growth follows expanded eligibility under recent legislation covering toxic exposure claims.

Army launches HVAC task force after heating and cooling tops barracks complaints

tags: defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Acting Army Secretary Adam Telle said working heat and air conditioning could resolve more than half of the service's barracks problems, speaking as the Army announced its first service-wide HVAC Task Force. Heating and cooling are now the top quality-of-life complaint among soldiers. The Army has directed $15 million toward 44 priority projects and identified more than $100 million in further potential work.

Former Chicago homicide detective identified as killer of 8-year-old in 1960 case

tags: legal
sources: @oafnation_actual

Chicago police say a former homicide detective, Thomas McInerney, murdered 8-year-old Gloria Kowalewicz in 1960. The case was solved 65 years later using DNA and a fingerprint found on the girl's purse, which matched prints McInerney submitted when applying to join the police department in 1959. He went on to investigate homicides himself and died in 2006 without facing charges.

Pope Leo diagnosed with lung cancer after surgery

tags: health
sources: @aaronparnas, @total.hypocrisy

Pope Leo has been diagnosed with adenocarcinoma of the lung and the lower lobe of his right lung has been removed, the Associated Press confirmed. The diagnosis was suspected from preoperative tests and confirmed during surgery, which was successful and free of complications. His prognosis is described as good and he has cancelled public appearances for the coming week.

Cornell found to have issued reprimands in most sexual assault cases

tags: legal
sources: @aaronparnas

A CNN investigation reported that Cornell University reviewed 51 sexual assault complaints between the mid-2020s and mid-2024, finding students responsible in at least 16 cases. Of those, two students were expelled and six suspended, while seven received written reprimands, probation, no-contact orders or "directed study," which can consist of reading a victim impact letter. The findings point to institutional failures in how the university disciplines students found responsible.

Free tool maps candidates who do not take AIPAC funding

tags: politics
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell

A website, voteforpeace.info, lets users select a state and see which state-level and federal candidates are not backed by AIPAC. The tool is presented as a resource for voters seeking candidates described as pro-peace, with Delia Ramirez of Illinois given as an example.

3D-printed plant-based meat heads to US grocery stores

tags: tech, markets
sources: @groundnews

Steakholder Foods is introducing five 3D-printed plant-based products under its Perfecta brand, including chicken breast, filet mignon, marbled steak, salmon patties and white fish patties, at retailers across the northeastern United States. Two varieties are listed on Instacart at $9.99 and $9.39, though neither was available for purchase in locations checked by Allrecipes. The products combine soy and pea proteins with fats and flavourings to replicate the texture of animal meat, and packaging does not identify them as 3D-printed.
